blocks.text: Inside a container, 127.0.0.1 is the container's private loopback, so the server must listen on 0.0.0.0 to receive published traffic; `-p` still controls what's exposed on the host.

$ docker run -p 8000:8000 rag-api uvicorn app.main:app      # default host 127.0.0.1
$ curl localhost:8000
curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
The symptom is "reset" or "empty reply", not "refused": docker-proxy accepts on the host, then can't connect to the container's eth0.

rows: One process per container, scale containers

items: Size from the CPU quota, not `os.cpu_count()` (host CPUs); set it explicitly.
Memory multiplies: each worker loads its own model.
CPU-bound embedding in `async def` blocks the loop: use `def`, run_in_threadpool, or a separate service.
Default trusted IP is 127.0.0.1, never the proxy in Docker, so headers are ignored → http:// redirects, proxy IP in logs, per-IP rate limits collapse.
`"*"` is only safe if the port is reachable solely via the proxy.

blocks.text: Q: "The app works inside the container but curl from the host gets connection reset. Why?" A: "It's listening on 127.0.0.1, the container's own loopback. Published traffic arrives on eth0, so bind to 0.0.0.0; the -p mapping decides host exposure."

items: Size workers from limits; memory scales with workers.
Trust forwarded headers only from the proxy's IPs.
Don't block the event loop with CPU work.
